clue.text: One well-liked at work that will have plenty of backing?

definitions.text: that will have plenty of backing?

parts.note: a firm is a business, a place of work
a favourite is a person liked above others

explanation.surface: A popular office colleague who can count on lots of support from co-workers.
explanation.walkthrough: The well-liked person comes 'at work', but in the answer the firm comes first; the question mark marks the betting sense of 'backing'.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing, the horse most heavily bet on, and unlikely to drift in the odds, is called this.

clue.text: One who is ill and not operable?

explanation.surface: A patient too sick for the surgeon to touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Stressed on the first syllable it is a sick person; stressed on the second it means void or not working.

clue.text: Large number — doesn't matter which, a large number

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
any means whichever one you like

explanation.surface: Someone shrugging that any big figure will do.
explanation.definitionFit: Many is a plain synonym for a great number of things.

clue.text: A beautiful woman describes Eastern ways

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round, so the goddess's name goes around the next letter

parts.note: Venus, goddess of love, stands for any beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A lovely woman gives an account of the customs of the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describes' is taken in its geometric sense of drawing a line round something, not of giving an account.
explanation.definitionFit: Avenues are routes or roads, and figuratively methods, both senses of ways.

clue.text: Begin song outdoors

parts.note: to open is to start something off
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: An instruction to strike up a song outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-air describes events held outside rather than under a roof.

clue.text: Charge for plant

explanation.surface: A fee levied on some vegetation.
explanation.definitionFit: To rush is to charge headlong; a rush is also a marsh plant with hollow stems.

clue.text: Thing to change into this evening

indicators.note: change tells us the letters of the two preceding words are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice on what outfit to put on later today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thing to change into' reads as clothing to put on; 'into' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight refers to the evening or night of the present day.

clue.text: Such an action may make Ian pretty upset with outfit

indicators.note: upset signals the letters of the two named words are knocked into a new order

parts.note: a suit is a set of clothes, an outfit

explanation.surface: Ian is put out by a pretty dress, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Action' is the legal sense of a lawsuit, and 'Such' points back to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A suit is a legal action, here one brought to establish who fathered a child.

clue.text: Account for all that talking?

parts.note: sounds like explaining a chatterbox, but an account is also a bill, here for phone calls

explanation.definitionFit: A phone company's invoice charges for the calls made, the cost of all that chat.

clue.text: Go ahead and give money maybe

explanation.surface: Permission to proceed and to hand over some cash.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance is to move forward; an advance is also money paid or lent before it is due.

clue.text: Concentration that's required when driving in France

definitions.text: that's required when driving in France

explanation.surface: A tip for motorists abroad: stay focused on the French roads.
explanation.walkthrough: Essence is the French word for petrol, which you need to drive a car there.
explanation.definitionFit: An essence is a concentrated extract; in French the word names gasoline fuel.

clue.text: Female union of the Spanish and the French

parts.note: el is the Spanish masculine article
la is the French feminine article

explanation.surface: A marriage joining Spanish and French families.
explanation.definitionFit: Ella is a woman's first name, standing for any female.

clue.text: A game between two sides back in the country

indicators.note: back tells us the whole assembled run is read in reverse
between places the article and the game inside the two sides

parts.note: left and right, L and R
RU is rugby union, a ball game

explanation.surface: A match between two teams being played again out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LARUR (A and RU between L and R) round.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural describes things located in the countryside rather than towns.

clue.text: Complaint that may be socially acceptable in time

indicators.note: in places the acceptable letter inside the word for time

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
U means upper-class, socially acceptable, in British usage

explanation.surface: Some grievance that would be acceptable to air in due course.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U were labels for upper-class and middle-class British speech habits.
explanation.definitionFit: Ague is an old word for a fever or malarial illness, a complaint in the medical sense.

clue.text: A Caledonian title of course

parts.note: taken as written
Caledonia is the Latin name for Scotland, so a Caledonian is a Scot

explanation.surface: A Scottish nobleman's rank, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' looks like 'naturally'; it means a racecourse. Ascot is the famous English racecourse in Berkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is the name of a celebrated racecourse, home of Royal Ascot.

clue.text: Surrounded by cultivated mango

indicators.note: cultivated suggests the fruit's letters have been worked over into a new form

explanation.surface: Fruit trees grown in an orchard, hemmed in on all sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Among means in the midst of, encircled by others.

clue.text: They don't like to assume anything

definitions.text: They don't like to assume anything

parts.words: They don't like to assume anything
parts.note: assume here means put on clothes, not take for granted

explanation.definitionFit: Naturists prefer to wear no clothes at all, so they put nothing on.

clue.text: About to get striker for return game

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a match is struck to light it

explanation.surface: A footballer's centre-forward comes into focus before a second fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' suggests a footballer; here it is a thing you strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A rematch is a second contest between the same opponents.

clue.text: Stop vessel caught in swell

indicators.note: caught in places the container word inside the word for a smart person

parts.note: a swell is an old word for a fashionable person, a toff
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: A boat halted when trapped by a large wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swell' looks like a sea wave but is the dated slang for a well-dressed gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn off a machine or tap is to stop it running.

clue.text: Sailor climbs rope — this one?

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
a line is a rope on a ship

explanation.surface: A seaman scales the rigging.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a ratline is one of the small ropes forming steps up a ship's shrouds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratlines are the rungs of rope sailors climb to go aloft.

clue.text: Natural cover in garden, originally

parts.note: the garden is Eden, where Adam and Eve first covered themselves with leaves

explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Adam and Eve sewed together leaves of a fig tree to cover their nakedness.

clue.text: Restaurant cutlery

explanation.surface: An eatery's knives and forks.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen is a workplace dining room, and also a boxed set of cutlery.

clue.text: One who cribs in an exam upsets teacher

definitions.text: One who cribs in an exam

indicators.note: upsets tells us the letters of the following word are disordered

explanation.surface: A pupil copying answers who annoys the invigilator.
explanation.definitionFit: To crib is to copy dishonestly, which is exactly what this sort of dishonest pupil does.

clue.text: Feeling I'm one to get pushed around

indicators.note: pushed around tells us the letters of the three preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who feels they are always being bullied.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotion is a feeling such as joy or anger.

clue.text: One of the first people named in Somerset House

definitions.text: One of the first people named

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies within the words that follow

explanation.surface: An early ancestor listed in the old register of births held at Somerset House.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerset House in London once held the register of births, marriages and deaths for England and Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Seth was the third son of Adam and Eve, among the earliest people named in the Bible.

clue.text: Makes eyes at the French on turning to leave

indicators.note: on places the French article after the turned word
turning tells us the word for leaving is reversed

parts.note: to go is to leave
les is the French plural article

explanation.surface: Flirting with French people while turning to walk away.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to stare at someone with desire, making eyes at them.

clue.text: Company doctor's card

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A business medic's appointment card or calling card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card' is a verb: to card wool is to comb out its fibres.
explanation.definitionFit: Carding and combing are both ways of disentangling fibres such as wool.

clue.text: Leading sea power

explanation.surface: A dominant naval nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Main means chief; the main is the open ocean; and main means strength, as in might and main.

clue.text: Bearded Asian with head wound?

parts.note: wound is the past of wind, so the head is wrapped in a turban, not injured

explanation.definitionFit: Observant men of this Punjabi faith leave their beards uncut and wind a turban about the head.

clue.text: Flatter most sincerely?

parts.note: from the saying that imitation is the sincerest form of flattery

explanation.definitionFit: To copy someone is, proverbially, the most sincere way of paying them a compliment.

clue.text: Four will make an appearance in test of little importance

indicators.note: make an appearance in signals the number turning up inside the test

parts.note: a trial is a test
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four people showing up for an unimportant examination.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trivial is petty or insignificant.

clue.text: Old coppers that went by foot

definitions.text: Old coppers that went by foot

parts.words: Old coppers that went by foot
parts.note: coppers are old copper coins, not police on the beat; the bicycle was pedalled by foot

explanation.walkthrough: The penny and the farthing (a quarter of a penny) were British copper coins before decimalisation.
explanation.definitionFit: This Victorian bicycle had a huge front wheel and a tiny rear one, named after two pre-decimal British coins.
